about: Exported from reproducibility/literature_evidence/evidence.json by scripts/export_app_evidence.py. Only records with an app factor are included; app/literature.js applies a record only if verified, provenance is "primary" and usable_in_app is true.

records.se_or_other: p < .01; no CI or SE printed. Per 1-point higher husband score on a 1-4 scale (mean of: yelled and shouted, insulted or called names, brought up things from long ago, had to have the last word). The same model carries a proportional-hazards correction "Hus. Destructive X Years to divorce" HR .14, i.e. the husband effect is time-varying and 4.28 is not a constant hazard ratio.
records.population: Early Years of Marriage Project, Wayne County MI, 47% White / 53% Black
records.adjusted_for: couple income, education, income ratio, premarital children, months cohabited, couple age, each spouse raised with 2 parents, race
records.citation: Birditt, K. S., Brown, E., Orbuch, T. L., & McIlvane, J. M. (2010). Marital conflict behaviors and implications for divorce over 16 years. Journal of Marriage and Family, 72(5), 1188-1204.
records.locator: Table 3 (Cox regression, Year 1 conflict behaviours; n = 207): columns Model 1 Block 1, Model 1 Block 2, Model 2, Model 3, Model 4; value = Model 1 Block 2
records.quote: Cox Regression Models Examining Divorce as a Function of Conflict Behaviors in Year 1 (n = 207) ... Destructive | | | | | ... Husband | | 4.28** | 6.37** | | ... Hus. Destructive X Years to divorce | | .14** | .13** | |
records.usable_withheld: Non-proportional: the paper adds a husband-destructive x time interaction (HR .14 per year) whose time scale/centring is not reported, so a constant HR of 4.28 would misstate it. Not applied.
records.caveats: Scale-unit HR (not standardised); time-varying effect for husband; self-report.

records.unit: per 1 point on the 1-4 destructive-behaviour scale

center.note: average of the printed Year 1 wife means (2.0 White, 2.2 Black; sample 47% White / 53% Black)

records.se_or_other: p < .05; no CI or SE printed. Per 1-point higher wife score on a 1-4 scale (same four items). Year 1 wife means printed in Table 2: 2.0 (White) and 2.2 (Black), SD .8. No time interaction reported for wives.
records.citation: Birditt, K. S., Brown, E., Orbuch, T. L., & McIlvane, J. M. (2010). Marital conflict behaviors and implications for divorce over 16 years. Journal of Marriage and Family, 72(5), 1188-1204.
records.locator: Table 3 (Cox regression, Year 1 conflict behaviours; n = 207): columns Model 1 Block 1, Model 1 Block 2, Model 2, Model 3, Model 4; value = Model 1 Block 2 (all four behaviour types for both spouses plus race, couple education, income, income ratio, premarital children, months cohabited, age at marriage, parents' family structure)

records.contrast: At least one spouse not religious vs other (married 1975+)
records.unit: at least one spouse reports no religion (reference: other religious combinations except both Catholic)
records.se_or_other: SE(B) = 0.101; estimate is the printed OR; 95% CI derived as exp(ln OR +/- 1.96 x SE) (not reported).
records.n: 6,309 couples (PSID); 1,303 divorces in 1975+ cohort, 381 in earlier cohort
records.population: US first-married different-sex couples, both 18-55, PSID (1975+ cohort)
records.adjusted_for: economic well-being, wife economic dependence, both spouses' FT employment, wife housework share, duration, religion, race, nativity, home ownership, children, premarital cohabitation/birth, age at marriage, each spouse's education, health, occupation/industry sex composition, region, marriage cohort
records.citation: Killewald, A. (2016). Money, work, and marital stability: Assessing change in the gendered determinants of divorce. American Sociological Review, 81(4), 696-719.
records.locator: Table 3 (logistic regression of marital dissolution, PSID; columns 1. Married in 1974 or Earlier, 2. Married in 1975 or Later, 3. Pooled). Each cell prints B, (SE), OR. Value = column 2
records.caveats: Annual hazard OR; covariates measured in prior year.

records.unit: correlation with divorce; converted to a per-SD log-odds in app/literature.js with an explicit base-rate assumption
records.se_or_other: 95% CI as printed. The PDF encodes the minus sign and "=" with private glyphs (extract as U+0001 and "5"); SOURCES.json records this glyph map.
records.adjusted_for: varies by study (fewer controls than health studies)
records.citation: Roberts, B. W., Kuncel, N. R., Shiner, R., Caspi, A., & Goldberg, L. R. (2007). The power of personality: The comparative validity of personality traits, socioeconomic status, and cognitive ability for predicting important life outcomes. Perspectives on Psychological Science, 2(4), 313-345.
records.locator: Text, section on divorce (meta-analytic average of prospective studies; correlations)
records.quote: When so aggregated, the effect of Neuroticism on divorce was .17 (CIs = .12 and .22), the effect of Agreeableness was −.18 (CIs = −.27 and −.09), and the effect of Conscientiousness on divorce was −.13 (CIs = −.17 and −.09). ... the relation between SES and divorce was −.05 (CIs = −.08 and −.02)
records.caveats: Correlations with a binary outcome; convert to OR via d (r->d->lnOR) with base rate care.

records.contrast: Major depression before marriage vs none (all disorders entered together)
records.unit: person had major depression before the marriage
records.n: WHO World Mental Health surveys, 12 countries with divorce timing
records.population: Ever-married adults in WHO World Mental Health surveys
records.design: retrospective survey, discrete-time survival (onset of disorder before marriage)
records.adjusted_for: sex, age, country, years since marriage, months dating prior to marriage, education, all other disorders
records.citation: Breslau, J., Miller, E., Jin, R., Sampson, N. A., Alonso, J., Andrade, L. H., ... Kessler, R. C. (2011). A multinational study of mental disorders, marriage, and divorce. Acta Psychiatrica Scandinavica, 124(6), 474-486.
records.locator: Table 4 "Association between premarital mental disorders and the age of first divorce in all countries" (discrete-time survival ORs; columns Model 1 individual disorders, Model 2 all disorders, Model 3 all disorders with number of disorders; controls: sex, age, country, years since marriage, months dating prior to marriage, education). Value = Model 2.
records.quote: Association between premarital mental disorders and the age of first divorce in all countries ... Major depression | 1.6 | 1.5, 1.8 | 1.6 | 1.4, 1.8 | 1.5 | 1.3, 1.7
records.caveats: Retrospective reports of disorder onset; cross-national pooled; individual-level (the respondent's own divorce). Model 2 adjusts all disorders simultaneously, which is the version used when several adjustments stack.

records.predictor: Premarital cohabitation with partners other than the eventual husband
records.contrast: Wife had one nonmarital cohabiting partner before marriage vs none
records.unit: wife cohabited with exactly one partner other than her husband before marrying
records.se_or_other: log-odds B = 1.11, SE = 0.03; OR = exp(B), 95% CI exp(B +/- 1.96 SE) derived (not printed).
records.population: U.S. women's first marriages, NSFG 1995-2015 waves
records.design: retrospective marital histories, discrete-time event history
records.adjusted_for: premarital cohabitation with husband (and its calendar-year interaction), marital duration, year of marriage, age at marriage, children, calendar decade, education, race, family of origin, mother's education, NSFG wave
records.citation: Rosenfeld, M. J., & Roesler, K. (2019). Cohabitation experience and cohabitation's association with marital dissolution. Journal of Marriage and Family, 81(1), 42-58.
records.locator: Table 3, Model 4 (log-odds coefficients, SE in parentheses; columns M1-M4)
records.caveats: Women only; strongly selected (people with more prior cohabitations differ in many ways). Model 4 has no cohort interaction, so it is an average over marriage cohorts. Author's posted manuscript (2018), published 2019.
